sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Horizon City
sections.html:
A broker, a private sale and a cash buyer are the usual choices. With owners in 85.2% of Horizon City homes, most sellers are families leaving a house they have called home.

Cash fits when you need a firm closing day or dread paying for repairs. A listing fits a house in good order and an owner who can wait out a buyer's loan. Do the same prep either way.

  • Collect the deed, your latest tax statement and any utility district bills.
  • Get each buyer's terms in writing, covering price, closing day and who pays what.
  • Request proof of funds before you take the house off the market.

sections.h2: How the town was laid out
sections.html:
The town lies roughly 15 miles east of El Paso, with the Franklin Mountains to the west. A Chicago-based developer announced the project in December 1959, and a planning firm from Tucson laid the town out beside the proposed Interstate 10 route. The first house sold on October 31, 1962. Horizon City incorporated on August 13, 1988, and voters adopted a charter in November 1997. It runs as a home rule city under a mayor and seven council members.

Harsh desert sun and dry air wear down roofs, stucco and paint, and inspectors look hard at cooling equipment. Fix the inexpensive items before a showing, or lower your price to account for what you leave.

Median value is $170,200 for 2020 to 2024. The 2025 head count of 25,118 is 11.8% above the 2020 base of 22,461, and that steady growth keeps new subdivisions coming, so expect competition from new builds.

The 3.39-person household means buyers often want extra bedrooms. A 29.4-minute average commute points to workers heading into El Paso, so access to Interstate 10 and Eastlake Boulevard is part of what you are selling.

The population is young: children are 33.7% of residents and seniors only 5.5%. And 92.5% of people stayed put for a year, a sign of settled families. Buyers tend to want extra bedrooms, a yard and a quick run to Interstate 10.

Language matters too, since about 73.5% of residents speak another language at home. If a relative who reads Spanish is helping with the sale, ask the buyer for the contract and disclosures in a form you can read before signing. A clean, working house with documented repairs draws more interest than one with open questions.

The council takes advice on zoning and development from a Planning and Zoning Commission and a Board of Adjustment. Did you add a room, fence, carport or pool? Ask town hall whether it was permitted, since lenders and title companies sometimes check.

A lot near the town's edge may sit in the county instead, which changes who issues permits and provides services, so confirm which. Buyers who care about traffic and walkability may also ask about plans for the street your house faces, such as Darrington Road or Eastlake Boulevard.

The Socorro and Clint school districts and the Horizon Regional Municipal Utility District serve the area. Buyers will want to know which district covers a home, and your tax bill answers that.

Every parcel of real property and business personal property in the county is appraised by the El Paso Central Appraisal District. Its home page links protests and appeals, exemption forms, a deadline calendar and a taxpayer liaison for complaints about the review board. Look at the calendar for the protest date that fits your notice.

  • Appraisal district: your value and exemptions.
  • County tax office: the bill and a payoff statement.
  • County clerk: deed and other recorded papers.
  • Town hall: permits, zoning and utility accounts.

Deeds are recorded by the El Paso County Clerk. Before a land deed is accepted for filing, the signer must acknowledge it to a notary or similar officer, or two witnesses must swear to it. Plan to sign with ID in hand.

Recording fees in the 2023 clerk manual run $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for each added page and $0.25 for every indexed name past five. Records fees add things like $2.00 for technology and up to $10 each for management and archive, and a missing grantee address can add $25. Fees change, so check the clerk's current schedule.

The title company usually files for you in the county where the land sits, El Paso County for a Horizon City house. The manual mentions no transfer tax. Each charge on your side appears on the settlement statement.

A tax lien for each year attaches to the land on January 1 and rides along through any sale. Even after a transfer a court can order the property sold, so clear title waits until delinquent taxes are paid.

A bill still open once January 31 is behind you counts as late, and charges begin February 1. When a house is auctioned for taxes, the former owner may buy it back: two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed for homestead, farm and mineral land, at a 25 percent markup in year one and 50 percent in year two, or 180 days for other land. A tax sale surplus can be claimed for two years.

Selling before anyone sues over back taxes spares you court costs. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure, and ask whether an installment plan is available, which some collectors grant on a residence homestead.

sections.h2: Before you list or accept a bid
sections.html:
Set aside an afternoon for paperwork before the first buyer walks in, and keep every document in one folder. Pull the deed, find any survey, and note which taxing units and which school district appear on your tax bill. Ask the tax office for the current balance so you know the exact figure that must be paid at the closing table.

Then walk the house with a notepad. Write down what works, what is worn out and what you would rather leave alone. Any buyer or inspector will find the same items, and an owner who names them first earns trust and tends to face fewer late price cuts.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html: Once under contract, the file moves to a title company that orders the search, requests payoffs and confirms taxes are current. You sign in front of a notary at closing, the deed is filed, and what is left after payoffs and charges is yours. No lender approval is needed with cash, which helps a firm date hold. Leave your utility district account open until closing day, then ask the buyer to move it into their name. Leave manuals, remotes and garage openers for the new owner, and take photos of the empty house for your own records.

faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 25,118, which is 11.8% higher than the 2020 base.

faqs.q: Will I owe a transfer tax?
faqs.a: The clerk's fee schedule shows recording charges but no transfer tax. Your title company can give you the full settlement statement.

faqs.q: Does a tax balance stop my sale?
faqs.a: No. The balance gets paid out of your proceeds at closing, because the lien stays with the house. The county tax office issues the payoff statement.

faqs.q: Who decides the value of my property for tax?
faqs.a: The El Paso Central Appraisal District. Its calendar lists protest dates, and its taxpayer liaison handles complaints.

faqs.q: Is $170,200 the price my house will fetch?
faqs.a: That is a townwide midpoint for 2020 to 2024. For your own address, rely on written offers or an appraisal.
